output.brief: FCR fell because of the 14 April Finance change, not the new starters. It cut the credit agents can give on a call from £100 to £25 and automatically refers larger cases to the Billing Resolution team. Referred billing calls went from 7% to 54%. Those customers call back about status, and their FCR is about 34%, against 82% for calls that aren't referred. The referral rate is the same for new and experienced agents (53–56%). Experienced agents' FCR fell from 75% to 67%, matching the new starters at 66%. The tariff mix shift and the IVR change don't explain the drop. The timing also fits the 14 April step. I'm fairly confident, though agent-level data is thin. Don't put the April intake on performance plans: they aren't the cause, and it would punish the wrong group. Next, agree a revised credit limit with Finance, with post-call sampling. Trial it on two teams for six weeks, tracking FCR and unsupported credits against Finance's 1% threshold. Ask MI for the breakdown by team, which takes about a day. Holding off a full rollout and the three-month dashboard rebuild is reasonable.
